Cards carry their data in HTML attributes (positionname, cityname, workmodeltext, jobdatestatus) rather than nested markup, so there is almost no selector surface to break. robots.txt permits /is-ilanlari/ and disallows only CV, profile, application and settings paths — none of which this touches. No login.

portals.label: Arbeitnow

Note there is NO visa_sponsorship field in the current payload despite what older write-ups claim — the visa signal comes from the description like every other source. Their terms ask for a link back, which the stored `url` provides.

portals.label: beBee
portals.status: Verified 2026-08-08 against live TR pages. Posting pages carry a full schema.org JobPosting (datePosted, structured addressLocality/ addressCountry, identifier), so there are no selectors at all. Constraint: robots.txt allows / but disallows every query parameter including ?page=, and the sitemap holds only category pages (0 individual postings out of 2394). So listings come from each page's own ld+json ItemList, which caps at 20 postings per country page with no way to reach the 21st. A shallow, frequent skim rather than a deep crawl.

portals.label: JobFluent
portals.status: Verified 2026-08-08. Not a Next.js site — no __NEXT_DATA__ and no ld+json — but it publishes schema.org *microdata* (itemprop) covering title, datePosted, addressLocality/addressCountry, hiringOrganization, identifier and a curated comma-separated `skills` list. So no invented selectors: every field is addressed by its schema.org property name. Listings come from the advertised sitemap, split by region (remote/barcelona/madrid/valencia); Barcelona alone lists 392 postings. robots.txt gives ClaudeBot/GPTBot/CCBot a blanket Disallow — those are bulk AI crawlers. The `User-agent: *` block covering this tool disallows only /login, /sessions*, /api/*, /track and the /*/external* apply redirects, none of which are touched.

portals.label: Ticjob
portals.status: Batch 3 2026-10-01: strict robots recon returned a redirect; no job endpoint fetched in this audit. Historical sitemap/JobPosting parser retained with salary period, skill/scope/expiry evidence. Specific job URL supplies identity, never the organization identifier. Current full detail access is unverified.

portals.label: Jobicy
portals.status: Verified 2026-08-08 via RSS, not the JSON API. The documented /api/v2/remote-jobs is forbidden by the site's own robots.txt (line 48, `Disallow: /api/`) and the scraper obeys it — the first attempt returned zero postings and no error. The RSS feed is a different, permitted path: `Disallow: /feed$` pins to the bare /feed and nothing covers /jobs/feed. The feed is richer than the API anyway, carrying company, location, job_type and category in a jobicy namespace; the only loss is the API's jobLevel field. geo and industry filters both work on it.

portals.label: RemoteOK
portals.status: Verified 2026-08-08, 100 postings. Free public JSON API, no key. robots.txt allows `*` and sets `Content-Signal: search=yes, ai-train=no, use=reference` — reference use is exactly this, and nothing here trains anything. (ClaudeBot and the other bulk AI crawlers are named and disallowed; this tool is neither.) The first array element is their API terms rather than a posting and is skipped. Terms require a followed link back, which the stored url provides. `location` is usually empty; the signal is in `tags` (dev, engineer, senior, python, react), surfaced into the description for the scorer. Carries real salary ranges, rare here.

portals.label: We Work Remotely
portals.status: Verified 2026-08-08. Public RSS feeds the site offers for this purpose, asking only for attribution back — the stored url provides it. robots is Allow:/ apart from account and admin paths. Key finding: the category feeds do NOT nest. "All Programming" returned 25 postings that appeared in none of the others, while Full-Stack had 123, DevOps 51, Back-End 29 and Front-End 16, all disjoint — fetching only the "all" feed would have collected 25 of 219. Every engineering category is fetched and merged; design, sales, support and management are left out.

portals.label: Wellfound
portals.status: Verified 2026-08-08. Next.js role pages ship their Apollo GraphQL cache in __NEXT_DATA__, so no selectors. Jobs hang off companies — a StartupResult lists its postings by __ref and the posting carries no company itself. Two fields nothing else here provides: yearsExperienceMin as a number stated by the poster, and real compensation including equity. Caveat: the page also loads Cloudflare and captcha machinery. It served fine at 2s with an honest UA, but this is the likeliest source to start refusing — if it does it will surface as an error run, and it should be left refused rather than worked around.

portals.label: Remote Rocketship
portals.status: Blocked at the door. robots.txt permits it, but the site answers 403 with a Cloudflare "Just a moment" challenge to an honest UA. Getting past that means impersonating a browser or routing around the challenge, which is not something this project does. No parser written.

portals.label: EuroTechJobs
portals.status: Verified 2026-08-08. robots names ClaudeBot/GPTBot/Bytespider with Disallow but leaves `User-agent: *` fully open, the same shape as JobFluent. No structured data anywhere and the sitemap holds only articles, so this needed real selectors, taken from a captured page: li.highlightedJobContainer and li.standardJobContainer, with h3, .companyName, .location, .postedDate and .badge inside. Both container classes are read — taking only one would drop either every promoted posting or nearly everything. postedDate is relative prose ("Posted 10 days ago") with no absolute timestamp, so date_source is `updated`, never `employer`.

portals.label: WeAreDevelopers
portals.status: Verified 2026-10-01: the site advertises /jobs.md and matching full-job Markdown via /agents.md. Bounded cursor listings use country=all, numeric IDs, stack/salary/seniority and explicit apply links. Board Published is updated provenance; Remote available is not worldwide eligibility. Up to 10 details per run, richness caps remain partial.

portals.label: Tecnoempleo
portals.status: Verified 2026-08-08. The advertised sitemap.xml is the offer index: 2,008 live postings (priority 1.0, real lastmod) — the search page's query parameters are undocumented and are never touched. Each offer page carries a schema.org JobPosting with a real datePosted, so date_source is employer; the ld+json identifier is the *company* id (the JobFluent trap), so external_id comes from the rf-<hex> URL tail. The sitemap also holds the site history back to 2017, so offers are filtered to the last max_age_days and fetched newest-first, capped at max_offers. Closed offers resolve to a search page without a JobPosting and are skipped. robots.txt disallows AnthropicBot/Claude*/GPTBot by name with a blanket Disallow: / — this tool is none of those and identifies honestly; the owner's stated intent is on record and the choice is deliberate.

portals.label: EURES
portals.defaults: (config: 'Any' = None, *, searches: 'Any' = None, countries: 'tuple[str, ...] | list[str] | None' = None, results_per_page: 'int' = 50) -> 'None'
portals.status: Verified 2026-08-08 — the largest source in the project. POST to /eures/api/jv-searchengine/public/jv-search/search. The service name was not guessable (eight plausible names all 401'd); it came from a captured request. Referer and Origin are required, but an honest forkjob/0.1 UA works — no browser impersonation. The captured sessionId is not needed. Occupations filter by ESCO URI rather than keyword, so ISCO C25 targets ICT roles directly across all 24 languages. numberRecords gives the total up front, so paging stops exactly. robots.txt has no rule against /eures but sets Crawl-delay: 10 — min_interval below enforces it, do not lower.

portals.label: HN Who is Hiring
portals.status: Verified 2026-08-09 against the August 2026 thread: 308 comments. Algolia's public API, no key, and hn.algolia.com serves no robots.txt at all; news.ycombinator.com itself is never fetched, only linked. Two threads are posted the same day by the same account and only one is employers — "Who wants to be hired?" is candidates advertising themselves, so the title filter is load-bearing. Only top-level comments are postings; replies are conversation. The pipe-separated first line is a convention rather than a schema, so each segment is classified by what it looks like, not by its position.

portals.label: Jobspresso
portals.status:
Verified 2026-08-09: 20 postings, all remote. WP Job Manager RSS. robots.txt allows it — the only broad rule is `Disallow: /*?`, which covers query strings, and this path has none; crawl-delay 3. Note the site's main /feed/ is the blog and carries no postings at all. Company and location are not separate elements: both are packed into dc:creator as "Company
pin Location", and postings list every country they hire from, so the country is taken from the first resolvable entry.

portals.label: JobTech (Platsbanken)
portals.status: Verified 2026-08-09: 290 postings over five English role searches, 116 of them in English. Open government data from Arbetsformedlingen, the Swedish public employment service — no key, no bot protection, and Swedish employers are required by law to post here, so it is the most complete view of one country's market in this registry. The API has no language filter and most postings are Swedish, so the language is detected from the description and stored on the job; searches are English role names because an English-titled ad at a Swedish employer is itself a signal about the working language.

portals.label: Custom RSS feeds
portals.status: Reads data/feeds.yaml, which the web UI at /feeds writes — adding a feed in the browser is enough for the next sync to collect it. Generic RSS 2.0 and Atom only, so what it extracts is the intersection of every feed: title, link, date, description. A board with a real API or its own quirks deserves a dedicated scraper instead. Feeds fail independently and each failure is reported by name, because a feed that returns nothing looks exactly like one that was never reachable. Ships with a single disabled example entry.

portals.label: No Fluff Jobs
portals.status: Verified bounded 2026-10-01: public search POST has explicit PLN/month query semantics and native IDs. Up to 20 public JobPosting details recover full prose, structured skill values, employer/type/scope and expiry when supplied. Null expiry remains unknown. Board posted/renewed timestamps are updated; listing and richness completeness separate.

Every non-remote posting carries relocation and visa sponsorship by the board's own premise, so that signal is stated rather than inferred.
